clue.text: Old cat eating head of ornamental Chinese duck

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside, so the old cat's letters swallow the rest

parts.note: pard is an archaic word for a leopard

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: opening letter of ornamental
standard abbreviation for Chinese

explanation.surface: A historic Chinese cat with an appetite for something decorative.
explanation.walkthrough: PARD (an old word for leopard) takes in O and CH to give P-OCH-ARD.
explanation.definitionFit: The pochard is a diving bird of the waterfowl family, a common European species with a chestnut head.

clue.text: See 18
Outgoing figure claiming virgin's first kiss

indicators.note: claiming means seizing and holding onto, so the figure takes the letter inside

parts.note: a cone is a solid geometric figure

indicators.note: first points to only the opening letter of the word

parts.note: opening letter of virgin
X is the conventional kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A sociable person snatches an innocent's first kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outgoing figure' looks like a sociable person; 'Outgoing' alone is the definition, meaning bulging outward.
explanation.definitionFit: A convex surface curves outwards, so in shape terms it goes out rather than in.

clue.text: Medic (female) wearing type of garment is something to get the pulse racing!

definitions.text: something to get the pulse racing

indicators.note: whoever wears a garment is inside it, so these letters go within

parts.note: an A-line is a skirt or dress flaring from the waist
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
Ena is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A female doctor in a striking outfit makes hearts beat faster.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets round 'female' look like an aside, but they hold a woman's name. An A-line is a dress or skirt that flares from the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenaline is the hormone released in excitement or fear, raising the heart rate.

clue.text: Cope admirably without large pin

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: to do well is to cope admirably
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Managing nicely without a big fastener.
explanation.walkthrough: DO WELL loses one L.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowel is a headless wooden or metal peg used to join pieces in carpentry.

clue.text: Extremely tender animal's foot

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the two end letters of tender
an otter is an example of an animal

explanation.surface: A remark about how very tender some creature's foot is.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after animal reads as 'has', joining the wordplay to the definition rather than making a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A trotter is the foot of a pig or sheep, especially when cooked and eaten.

clue.text: Care for leader of rugby team forced into temporary accommodation

indicators.note: into places these letters inside the accommodation
forced suggests letters pushed out of shape into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written
a tent is a temporary shelter

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

parts.note: opening letter of rugby

explanation.surface: Looking after a rugby captain whose team has been squeezed into a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of rugby team' reads as a captain, but only the rugby letter is selected; the team's own letters are what get forced.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is medical attention for a patient, so it can stand for the noun care.

clue.text: German leaving animals out to grass

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that letter goes away
out reinforces that the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: goats are example animals
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A German farmer puts livestock out to pasture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out to grass' reads as a single phrase for retirement or pasture, but 'grass' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The oat plant is a cereal species, a cultivated member of the grass family.

clue.text: Colonel stopping riot waving republican flag

indicators.note: waving moves things to and fro, shifting the letters about
something stopping a gap plugs it, sitting in the middle

parts.note: the fodder rearranged
Col is the abbreviation for Colonel
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: An army officer quells rioters waving a revolutionary banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Republican flag' looks like a single definition, as the French tricolour is; the R comes from 'republican'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricolor is a banner of three bands of colour, such as the national ensign of France or Ireland.

clue.text: List of soldiers from different countries with incomplete time served

indicators.note: incomplete means missing its end, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
GIs are American soldiers, so the two sets come from different nations
a term is a period served, as in prison or office

explanation.surface: A roll of foreign troops who did not finish their tour of duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers from different countries' gives two sets: RE are British Royal Engineers and GIS American troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A register is an official record or roll of names, so it serves as a noun for a list.

clue.text: Hermit taking first instalment of annuity from mortgage provider?

indicators.note: taking something from a word removes it, leaving the rest behind

parts.note: a lender of a mortgage is, whimsically, a loaner; hence the question mark

indicators.note: the first instalment of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter of annuity

explanation.surface: A recluse draws the first payment of an annuity from the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A from LOANER to leave LONER.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit lives alone and shuns company, which is exactly what a solitary person does.

clue.text: Fighting faction holding line after period of inactivity

indicators.note: something that holds keeps another thing within its grasp, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a wing is a faction of a political party

indicators.note: after places the line's letter behind the inactive period in sequence

parts.note: a rest is time spent idle
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A political faction gets back into the fray after a quiet spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The faction holds both the inactive period and the line, which come in that order inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrestling is grappling combat, so as a verb form it can stand for fighting or struggling.

clue.text: Conservative slants overdue a fresh start

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
to slant is to lean to one side
overdue means late

explanation.surface: A Tory's biased views are long overdue a reset.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the usual abbreviation for Conservative, Britain's party of the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting with a clean slate is an idiom for beginning anew with past mistakes wiped away.

clue.text: 'Plant' in security service denied promotion

indicators.note: being denied something means going without it, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: Mossad is Israel's intelligence agency
an ad promotes a product

explanation.surface: A spy, or 'plant', inside an intelligence service is passed over for promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' in quotes looks like a mole in the spy sense; it is the botanical definition. MOSSAD loses AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Moss is a small flowerless green growth, a simple member of the vegetable kingdom.

clue.text: Garbled message about British Library getting article for collection

indicators.note: a garbled text is jumbled up, so the letters come out in a muddled order
about means around, so the jumbled letters surround the next pieces

parts.note: the fodder rearranged

indicators.note: getting means acquiring something extra, adding it alongside

parts.note: BL is the abbreviation for the British Library
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A scrambled note concerning the national library obtains an item for its holdings.
explanation.walkthrough: BL plus A sits inside the reshuffled message: ASSEM-BLA-GE.
explanation.definitionFit: An assemblage is a gathering of things or people brought together, much like a collection.

clue.text: Ten boys learn about part of Irish folklore

indicators.note: about suggests letters turned around and moved here and there into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A group of schoolboys being taught Irish legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Kissing the stone at Blarney Castle in County Cork is said to confer the gift of persuasive talk, a famous legend.

clue.text: Revolution declared by maiden joining the French party held up as guide to good behaviour

indicators.note: joining sets one piece next to another in sequence
something declared is spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a roll is a turn or revolution
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: in a down entry, held up means lifted from bottom to top, so read upwards

parts.note: le is French for the
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A revolutionary declaration as a maiden joins a French party, upheld as an example of good conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M. LE and DO are read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is someone whose conduct others copy, making that person an exemplar for proper conduct.

clue.text: Beetroot and apple is cooked with legume

indicators.note: cooked means mixed and transformed, so the letters are stirred into a new order
the root of a plant is at its bottom, and in a down entry the bottom is the final letter

parts.note: read as beet's root: the bottom letter of beet in a down entry
the fodder, taken as written; and joins it on

explanation.surface: A recipe: beetroot and apple prepared together with a pulse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetroot' looks like the vegetable, but it splits into 'Beet' and 'root', the root being its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A split pea is a dried pea halved for cooking, and peas are pod-bearing plants in the legume family.

clue.text: Grassland beyond old city on the banks of Euphrates

parts.note: past means beyond
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city

indicators.note: a river's banks are its two edges, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of Euphrates

explanation.surface: Fields lie past an ancient city by the Euphrates.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur really did stand near the Euphrates, so the surface is geographically sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastures are fields of grass where livestock graze, so the plural noun means grassland.

clue.text: Tipsy cops pile in the local with less conspicuous colleagues

indicators.note: a tipsy person staggers about, so the letters lurch out of their order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Drunken uniformed officers crowd into the pub alongside their undercover colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: The local is British slang for one's nearest pub. The definition reads as colleagues of the cops in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Officers out of uniform blend in with the public, so they are the less noticeable members of the force.

clue.text: Publicity surrounding animal on ark?

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing on all sides, so the animal goes inside

parts.note: an ad is publicity
a boar is a wild pig

explanation.surface: A notice advertising the creatures on Noah's vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: a creature on the ark was aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard means on a ship or vessel, which is where every passenger on Noah's ark found itself.

clue.text: Almost swallow sticky stuff in drink

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to neck is slang for swallowing a drink quickly
tar is a sticky black substance

explanation.surface: Barely managing to gulp down something gooey in a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: To neck a drink is British slang for downing it quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar is the drink of the gods in myth, and more loosely any delicious beverage or fruit juice.

clue.text: Cypriot agreeing to carry letter from Greece

indicators.note: the words carry the answer within them, bearing it across their join

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A Cypriot consents to deliver some post sent from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth character of the Greek alphabet, so it is a letter originating there.

clue.text: In a prom bible bashing is unlikely

indicators.note: bashing knocks things about, battering the letters into a different shape

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone thumping the Bible at a Proms concert would be a strange sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'In' only sets the scene; the fodder is the ten letters of 'a prom bible'. The Proms are a London summer season of classical concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: Improbable describes something with little chance of happening, the same sense as unlikely.

clue.text: Ginger squirrels principally eating English plants

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside

parts.note: ginger hair is called red
E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, pointing at the first letter only

parts.note: opening letter of squirrels

explanation.surface: Red squirrels nibbling native vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ginger squirrels' paints the red squirrel, Britain's native species; RED takes E inside and S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are tall waterside grasses, a kind of plant growing in marshes.

clue.text: Boycott involving recipe for breakfast cereal

indicators.note: involving means including within, so the letter is placed inside

parts.note: to boycott is to ban
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin

explanation.surface: Refusing to buy anything containing a recipe for the morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for recipe, the Latin 'take' heading old prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran is the husk of grain, eaten as flakes in the morning for its fibre.

clue.text: Carriage returned with saddle for bird

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the carriage is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a trap is a light two-wheeled horse carriage
a saddle is a ridge between two peaks; with simply adds it

explanation.surface: A horse-drawn carriage brought back along with a saddle, for a rider.
explanation.walkthrough: The saddle here is the mountain kind, a dip-shaped ridge, not the horse kind the carriage suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a plump game species of the pheasant family, shot for sport.

clue.text: Estranged parent returning pictures

indicators.note: something returning heads back, so the parent's short form is read from right to left

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
pictures collectively are art

explanation.surface: An alienated father comes home to look at the photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple living separately after a falling-out are estranged, no longer together.

clue.text: Letter almost mailed to a liberal magazine

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of it, so the final letter goes

parts.note: ar is the spelt-out name of the letter R
mailed means sent
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: Someone almost posts a letter to a left-leaning periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' looks like a periodical, but here it means a weapons store. Letters are sometimes spelt out by name, as AR for R.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine in the military sense is a store for arms and ammunition, which is what an arsenal is.

clue.text: Slight winds from the east returning over centre of London

indicators.note: over here means spread across and around, enclosing what follows
in an across entry, coming back from the east means reading right to left

parts.note: to reel is to wind a line in

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so just the two central letters are kept

parts.note: the middle two letters of London

explanation.surface: Light easterly breezes blow back across central London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winds' looks like weather; it is the verb, as in winding a fishing line in.
explanation.definitionFit: Slight and slender both describe something thin, small or meagre in build or amount.
